variables.Rc: the coverage ratio, used to relate the force per unit width of discrete reinforcement to the force per unit width required across the entire structure; Rc = 1 in the case of continuous reinforcement, i.e., each reinforcement layer covers the entire horizontal surface of the reinforced soil zone (p. 3-13)
variables.b: the gross width of the strip, sheet, or grid; for grids, b is measured from the center to center of the outside longitudinal bars as shown in Figure 3-3
variables.Sh: center-to-center horizontal spacing between strips, sheets, or grids

printed_equations.formula: Pr = F* α σ′v Le C

variables.Pr: the pullout resistance at each of the reinforcement levels per unit width of reinforcement
variables.Le C: the total surface area per unit width of the reinforcement in the resistive zone behind the failure surface
variables.Le: the embedment or adherence length in the resisting zone behind the failure surface
variables.C: the reinforcement effective unit perimeter; e.g., C = 2 for and sheets, and because the edges are neglected C = 2 for strips and grids (as printed, p. 3-16)
variables.α: a scale effect correction factor to account for a non linear stress reduction over the embedded length of highly extensible reinforcements, based on laboratory data (generally 1.0 for metallic reinforcements and 0.6 to 1.0 for geosynthetic reinforcements, see Table 3-6); in the absence of test data, α = 0.8 for geogrids and α = 0.6 for geotextiles (extensible sheets) is recommended (p. 3-16)
variables.σ′v: the effective vertical stress at the soil-reinforcement interfaces

printed_equations.notes: The definition of C is printed "C = 2 for and sheets" (p. 3-16): a word is missing in the print; it is kept as printed.

printed_equations.formula: F* = Passive Resistance + Frictional Resistance, or, F* = Fq · αβ + tan ρ

variables.Fq: the embedment (or surcharge) bearing capacity factor
variables.αβ: a bearing factor for passive resistance which is based on the thickness per unit width of the bearing member

printed_equations.notes: The page prints "F* = Passive Resistance + Frictional Resistance" as text and then the numbered equation "or, F* = Fq · αβ + tan ρ" (p. 3-19). The parameters are summarized in Table 3-6 and Figure 3-4.

printed_equations.formula: F* = tan ρ = 1.2 + log Cu at the top of the structure = 2.0 maximum

variables.F*: the pullout resistance factor for steel ribbed reinforcement
variables.Cu: the uniformity coefficient of the backfill (D60/D10)

printed_equations.notes: Printed in bold after the equations (p. 3-20): if the specific Cu for the wall backfill is unknown at design time, a Cu = 4 should be assumed (i.e., F* = 1.8 at the top of the wall) for reinforced fills meeting the requirements of Section 3.1 of this chapter.

printed_equations.formula: F* = tan φ at a depth of 20 ft (6 m) and below

variables.F*: the pullout resistance factor for steel ribbed reinforcement
variables.φ: the peak friction angle of the soil, which for MSE walls using select granular backfill is taken as a maximum of 34 degrees unless project specific test data substantiates higher values (p. 3-21)

printed_equations.formula: F* = Fq αβ = 40 αβ = 40 (t/2St) = 20 (t/St) at the top of the structure

variables.F*: the pullout resistance factor for steel grid reinforcements with transverse spacing St ≥ 6 inches (150 mm) (p. 3-20)
variables.αβ: the contributing bearing (bearing factor for passive resistance)
variables.t: the thickness of the transverse bar
variables.St: the spacing of the transverse grid elements; St must be uniform throughout the length of the reinforcement rather than having transverse grid members concentrated only in the resistant zone; the maximum St distance is 24 in. (610 mm)

printed_equations.notes: For sloping backfills see Figure 4-15 (p. 3-21).

printed_equations.formula: F* = Fq αβ = 20 αβ = 20 (t/2St) = 10 (t/St) at a depth of 20 ft (6 m) and below

variables.F*: the pullout resistance factor for steel grid reinforcements with transverse spacing St ≥ 6 inches (150 mm) (p. 3-20)
variables.αβ: the contributing bearing (bearing factor for passive resistance)
variables.t: the thickness of the transverse bar
variables.St: the spacing of the transverse grid elements (24 in. (610 mm) maximum)

variables.F*: the pullout resistance factor for geosynthetic (geogrid and geotextile) sheet reinforcement, in the absence of test data (conservative)
variables.φ: the peak friction angle of the soil, which for MSE walls using select granular backfill is taken as a maximum of 34 degrees unless project specific test data substantiates higher values; for RSS structures it is normally established by test, a lower bound value of 28 degrees often being used (p. 3-21)

variables.ρ: the interface friction angle, determined from soil-geosynthetic direct shear tests in accordance with ASTM D 5321; the equation is for geotextiles, geogrids and geonet type drainage composites in the absence of test results
variables.φ: the friction angle of the soil

printed_equations.notes: As printed (p. 3-21). The sentence before it calls the quantity "the interface friction coefficient tan ρ" and says it "can be conservatively taken as" the equation, which is printed with ρ, not tan ρ, on its left side. Other geosynthetics such as geomembranes and some geocomposite drain cores may have much lower interface values and should be tested.

variables.Ec: the thickness of the reinforcement at the end of the design life
variables.ER: the sacrificial thickness of metal expected to be lost by uniform corrosion during the service life of the structure

printed_equations.formula: Tal = Fy Ac / b   (in strength per unit reinforcement width {kips/ft})

variables.Tal: the nominal long-term tensile strength of the reinforcement (force per unit width)
variables.Ac: design cross section area of the steel, defined as the original cross section area minus corrosion losses anticipated to occur during the design life of the wall (p. 3-23)
variables.b: the gross width of the strip, sheet or grid (see Figure 3-5)

printed_equations.formula: Ptal = Fy Ac   (in strength per reinforcement element {kips})

variables.Ptal: the tensile strength of a known steel or grid reinforcement expressed in terms of the tensile load carried by the reinforcement
variables.Ac: design cross section area of the steel, defined as the original cross section area minus corrosion losses anticipated to occur during the design life of the wall (p. 3-23)

printed_equations.formula: Tal = Tult / RF = Tult / (RFID × RFCR × RFD)   (in strength per unit reinforcement width)

variables.Tult: Ultimate Tensile Strength (strength per unit width); determined from wide strip tests per ASTM D4595 (geotextiles) or D6637 (geogrids) based on the minimum average roll value (MARV) for the product
variables.RF: Reduction Factor; the product of all applicable reduction factors
variables.RFID: Installation Damage Reduction Factor; accounts for the damaging effects of placement and compaction of soil or aggregate over the geosynthetic during installation; a minimum reduction factor of 1.1 should be used to account for testing uncertainties (p. 3-29)
variables.RFCR: Creep Reduction Factor; accounts for the effect of creep resulting from long-term sustained tensile load applied to the geosynthetic
variables.RFD: Durability Reduction Factor; accounts for the strength loss caused by chemical degradation (aging) of the polymer used in the geosynthetic reinforcement (e.g., oxidation of polyolefins, hydrolysis of polyesters, etc.)

variables.Tal: the nominal long-term tensile strength, evaluated without product specific data
variables.Tult: Ultimate Tensile Strength (strength per unit width)
variables.RF: Reduction Factor (Preliminary Design Reduction Factor, Section 3.5.2.g), 7

printed_equations.notes: For preliminary design of permanent structures or for applications defined by the user as not having severe consequences should poor performance or failure occur (p. 3-39). RF = 7 should be limited (i.e., do not use Eq. 3-13 where the requirements are not met) to projects where: granular soils (sands, gravels) are used in the reinforced volume; 4.5 ≤ pH ≤ 9; site temperature < 85° F (30° C); maximum backfill particle size of ¾-inch (19 mm); maximum MSEW height is 35 ft (10 m) and maximum RSS height is 50 ft (15 m) (p. 3-39); and for products meeting the minimum requirements in Table 3-13 (p. 3-40). For temporary applications not having severe consequences, a default value for RF of 3.5 rather than 7 may be considered (p. 3-40).

variables.Kab: active earth pressure coefficient for the retained backfill (vertical wall, horizontal backslope)

printed_equations.formula: Kab = sin²(θ + φ′b) / [Γ sin²θ sin(θ − δ)]

variables.Kab: active coefficient of earth pressure for near vertical walls (a face batter of less than 10 degrees from vertical) and a sloping backfill
variables.β: Nominal slope of backfill behind wall (deg)
variables.δ: Angle of friction between retained backfill and reinforced soil, set equal to β (deg)
variables.φ′b: effective friction angle of retained backfill (deg)
variables.θ: 90° for vertical, or near (< 10°) vertical, wall (deg)

printed_equations.formula: Γ = [1 + √( sin(φ′b + δ) sin(φ′b − β) / (sin(θ − δ) sin(θ + β)) )]²

variables.β: Nominal slope of backfill behind wall (deg)
variables.δ: Angle of friction between retained backfill and reinforced soil, set equal to β (deg)
variables.φ′b: effective friction angle of retained backfill (deg)
variables.θ: 90° for vertical, or near (< 10°) vertical, wall (deg)

variables.RR: the factored resistance against failure by sliding
variables.φτ: resistance factor for shear resistance between soil and foundation (equal to 1.0 for sliding of soil-on-soil, see Table 4-5)
variables.Rτ: nominal sliding resistance between reinforced fill and foundation soil

variables.F1: the retained backfill resultant (wall with horizontal backslope, Figure 4-2)
variables.Kab: active earth pressure coefficient for the retained backfill
variables.γb: moist unit weight of the retained backfill soil

variables.F2: the resultant for a uniform surcharge
variables.Kab: active earth pressure coefficient for the retained backfill

variables.FT: nominal retained backfill force resultant per unit width (wall with sloping backfill, Figure 4-3)
variables.Kab: active earth pressure coefficient for the sloping backfill, see Eq. 4-2
variables.γb: moist unit weight of the retained backfill soil
variables.h: total height of wall, H, and slope at the back of the reinforced zone = H + L tan β

printed_equations.notes: For a broken backslope (see Figure 4-4), h - H should not exceed the height of the upper crest. If the broken backslope height is defined as "S", then (H + L tanβ) ≤ (H + S); use (H + S) if (L tanβ) > S (p. 4-20).
The nominal horizontal driving force for a horizontal backslope and uniform live load surcharge (p. 4-20).

variables.Pd: the factored horizontal driving force (horizontal backslope and uniform live load surcharge)

printed_equations.notes: Use the maximum EH load factor (= 1.50) in these equations because it creates the maximum driving force effect for the sliding limit state (p. 4-21).
For a sloping backfill condition (p. 4-21).

printed_equations.formula: Pd = γEH FH = γEH FT cosβ

variables.Pd: the factored horizontal driving force (sloping backfill)

printed_equations.notes: Use the maximum EH load factor (= 1.50) in these equations because it creates the maximum driving force effect for the sliding limit state (p. 4-21).

variables.Rr: the factored resisting force per unit length of wall (horizontal backslope and uniform live load surcharge; the live load is excluded since it increases sliding stability)
variables.μ: minimum soil friction angle φ [tan φ′f, tan φ′r, or (for continuous reinforcement) tan ρ] (p. 4-22)

printed_equations.notes: Use the minimum EV load factor (= 1.00) in these equations because it results in minimum resistance for the sliding limit state (p. 4-22).

variables.Rr: the factored resisting force per unit length of wall (sloping backfill)
variables.μ: minimum soil friction angle φ [tan φ′f, tan φ′r, or (for continuous reinforcement) tan ρ] (p. 4-22)

printed_equations.notes: External loads that increase sliding resistance should only be included if those loads are permanent. Use the minimum EV load factor (= 1.00) in these equations because it results in minimum resistance for the sliding limit state (p. 4-22).

variables.e: the eccentricity, the distance between the resultant foundation load and the center of the reinforced zone (i.e., L/2) (Figure 4-7)
variables.ΣMD, ΣMR: the overturning and the resisting moments about the bottom, center of the base length

variables.e: the eccentricity for a vertical wall, with horizontal backslope and uniform live load surcharge (Figure 4-7)

printed_equations.formula: e = [γEH-MAX FT cosβ (h/3) − γEH-MAX FT sinβ (L/2) − γEV-MIN V2 (L/6)] / [γEV-MIN V1 + γEV-MIN V2 + γEH-MAX FT sinβ]

variables.e: the eccentricity beneath a wall with a sloping backfill, and no surcharges, with factored loads (Figure 4-8)

printed_equations.notes: Eccentricity check criteria (p. 4-23): e is acceptable if the resultant vertical force (based on factored loads) is within the middle one-half of the base width for soil foundations (i.e., emax = L / 4) and middle three-fourths of the base width for rock foundations (i.e., emax = 3/8 L).

variables.qR: the factored bearing resistance of the foundation soil
variables.quniform: the factored vertical pressure at the base of the wall, as calculated with the uniform Meyerhof-type distribution

variables.L: width of foundation, equal to reinforcement length L
variables.eB: eccentricity for bearing calculation (not equal to eccentricity check e)

printed_equations.formula: eB = [γEH-MAX F1 (H/3) + γLS Fq-LS (H/2)] / (γEV-MAX V1 + γLS q L)
printed_equations.notes: Where terms were previously defined. The maximum load factors for γEH and γEV are used to be consistent with the computation for σv where maximum load factors results in the maximum vertical stress. When eB is negative, a value of 0 should be carried forward in the design stress equation, i.e., set L′ = L, per AASHTO C11.10.5.4 (2007) (p. 4-27).

variables.σV-F: the factored vertical stress at the base assuming Meyerhof-type distribution (horizontal backslope and uniform live load surcharge)

printed_equations.formula: qV-F = (γEV-MAX V1 + γEV-MAX V2 + γEH-MAX FT sinβ) / (L − 2eB)

variables.qV-F: the factored bearing pressure for a wall with sloping backfill

printed_equations.notes: Note that (L – 2eB) is set equal to L when the value of eccentricity is negative (p. 4-28).

printed_equations.formula: qn = cf Nc + 0.5 L′ γf Nγ

variables.qn: the nominal bearing resistance, Equation 10.6.3.1.2a-1 of AASHTO (2007), for a level grade in front of a MSE wall and no groundwater influence
variables.cf: the cohesion of the foundation soil
variables.γf: the unit weight of the foundation soil
variables.L′: effective foundation width, equal to L – 2eB; set L′ equal to L if eB is a negative value

variables.φ: resistance factor, for MSE walls this factor is 0.65 (Table 11.5.6-1, AASHTO {2007})

variables.γr: the nominal unit weight of the reinforced fill
variables.cu: the nominal total stress cohesion of the foundation soil

printed_equations.notes: To prevent local shear of structures bearing on weak cohesive soils (p. 4-30).

variables.Ka: the active earth pressure coefficient for a vertical wall (the Rankine equation)
variables.φ′r: friction angle of the reinforced wall fill (engineering properties of the reinforced soil volume, γr, φ′r, p. 4-9)

printed_equations.formula: Ka = sin²(θ + φ′r) / {sin³θ [1 + sin φ′r / sin θ]}

variables.Ka: the active earth pressure coefficient for wall face batters equal to or greater than 10° from the vertical (simplified form of the Coulomb equation)
variables.θ: the inclination of the back of the facing as measured from the horizontal starting in front of the wall, as shown in Figure 4-5
variables.φ′r: friction angle of the reinforced wall fill

printed_equations.notes: Typed as printed on p. 4-36: the bracket in the denominator carries no exponent.

variables.σH: the horizontal stress at any given depth within the reinforced soil zone
variables.Kr: the coefficient of lateral earth pressure in the reinforced soil zone, obtained from Figure 4-10
variables.σv: the factored vertical pressure at the depth of interest
variables.ΔσH: the supplemental factored horizontal stress due to external surcharges (printed Δσh in the definition, p. 4-40)

variables.σH: the horizontal stress at any given depth Z below the top of the reinforced soil zone (MSE wall with level backfill and no surcharge)
variables.γr: the unit weight of soil in the reinforced soil zone
variables.Z: depth below the top of the reinforced soil zone
variables.γEV-MAX: the maximum load factor (= 1.35) for load type "EV"

variables.σH: the horizontal stress at any depth Z below the top of the reinforced soil zone (MSE wall with sloping backfill)
variables.Seq: height of the equivalent uniform soil surcharge by which the sloping surcharge is approximated (Figure 4-11)

variables.σH: the horizontal stress at any depth Z below the top of the reinforced soil zone (MSE wall with level backfill and live load surcharge)
variables.heq: height of the equivalent uniform soil surcharge representing the live load (equal to 2 ft)

printed_equations.formula: σH = Kr [γr (Z + h + heq) γEV-MAX + (Δσv-footing) γP-ES] + (ΔσH) γP-ES

variables.σH: the horizontal stress at any depth Z below the top of the reinforced soil zone (bridge abutment with a spread footing on top of MSE wall)
variables.h: the height of the roadway fill above the reinforced soil zone
variables.heq: equivalent uniform soil surcharge height of the live load, as per Table 4-4
variables.Δσv, ΔσH: the vertical (normal) and horizontal (shear) pressures at the bottom of the spread footing
variables.γP-ES: 1.50 if nominal (i.e., unfactored) pressures are used, and 1.00 if factored pressures are used, the final value being chosen based on larger values of (Δσv-footing)γP-ES and (ΔσH)γP-ES

printed_equations.formula: TMAX = σH Sv   (in force per unit reinforcement width {kips/ft})

variables.TMAX: the maximum factored tension in each reinforcement layer per unit width of wall
variables.σH: calculated at the level of the reinforcement, at the center of the contributory height
variables.Sv: the vertical reinforcement spacing for a layer where vertically adjacent reinforcements are equally spaced from the layer under consideration

variables.Rc: ratio of gross width of strip, sheet, or grid to the center-to-center horizontal spacing between the strips, sheets, or grids (see Eq. 3-9 and Figure 3-3); e.g., Rc = 1 for full coverage reinforcement

printed_equations.notes: The definition of Rc refers to "Eq. 3-9" (p. 4-47); the coverage ratio is Eq. 3-1 (p. 3-12), and Eq. 3-9 is the interface friction of geosynthetics. Kept as printed.

variables.PTMAX-D: maximum factored load in discrete reinforcement element (per panel width, for discrete reinforcements of known spacing and segmental precast concrete facing of known panel dimensions)
variables.NP: number of discrete reinforcements per panel width (e.g., 2, 3, etc.)

variables.Tal: the nominal long-term reinforcement design strength (Section 3.5)

printed_equations.notes: Tal and Tr may be expressed in terms of strength per unit width of wall, per reinforcement element, or per unit reinforcement width (p. 4-48).

variables.TMAX: the maximum factored load in a reinforcement (Eqs. 4-32)

printed_equations.formula: φ Le ≥ TMAX / (F* α σv C Rc)

variables.Le: The length of embedment in the resisting zone; the boundary between the resisting and active zones may be modified by concentrated loadings
variables.φ: Resistance factor for soil reinforcement pullout (Table 4-7)
variables.F*: Pullout resistance factor (see Chapter 3) with variation in depth starting at the same elevation as that for Kr/Ka variation
variables.σv: Nominal (i.e., unfactored) vertical stress at the reinforcement level in the resistant zone, including distributed dead load surcharges, neglecting traffic loads (Figure 4-15 for sloping backfills)
variables.C: 2 for strip, grid, and sheet type reinforcement

printed_equations.formula: Le ≥ TMAX / (φ F* α σv C Rc) ≥ 3 ft (1 m)

variables.Le: the required embedment length in the resistance zone (i.e., beyond the potential failure surface)

printed_equations.notes: If a traffic or other live load is present, it is recommended that TMAX be computed with the live loads and that the pullout resistance be computed excluding the live loads (p. 4-51).

variables.L: the total length of reinforcement required for internal stability
variables.La: obtained from Figure 4-9 for simple structures not supporting concentrated external loads such as bridge abutments
for MSE walls with extensible reinforcement, vertical face and horizontal backfill
variables.Z: the depth to the reinforcement level

variables.La: for the lower half of a wall with inextensible reinforcements, vertical face and horizontal backfill
for the upper half of a wall with inextensible reinforcements, vertical face, and horizontal backfill

variables.Talc: nominal long-term reinforcement/facing connection strength per unit reinforcement width at a specified confining pressure
variables.Tult: ultimate tensile strength of the geosynthetic soil reinforcement, defined as the minimum average roll value (MARV)
variables.RFD: reduction factor to account for chemical and biological degradation
variables.CRcr: long-term connection strength reduction factor to account for reduced ultimate strength resulting from the connection

variables.Tcrc: the creep reduced connection strength at the specified design life, from long-term connection creep tests
variables.Tlot: the ultimate wide width tensile strength of the reinforcement material roll/lot used for the connection strength testing

printed_equations.notes: CRcr defined with long-term testing (p. 4-54).

variables.Tultconn: an ultimate connection strength at a specified confining pressure, from short-term (i.e., quick) ultimate strength tests per ASTM D6638
variables.RFcr: the geosynthetic creep reduction factor (see Chapter 3)
variables.Tlot: the ultimate wide width tensile strength of the reinforcement material roll/lot used for the connection strength testing

printed_equations.notes: CRcr defined with short-term testing (p. 4-55).

variables.D15(filter), D85(soil): particle sizes of the filter and of the upstream soil

printed_equations.notes: The soil filtration criterion to prevent piping (i.e., retention) of the upstream soil into the filter (p. 5-25).

variables.D15(filter), D15(soil): particle sizes of the filter and of the upstream soil

printed_equations.notes: To ensure sufficient permeability of the filter material. For CL and CH soils without sand or silt particles, the D15 size of the filter in Equation 5-2 may be as great as 0.016 in, and Equation 5-3 may be disregarded (p. 5-25).

variables.D50(filter), D50(soil): particle sizes of the filter and of the upstream soil

printed_equations.notes: An additional criterion to prevent movement of soil particles into or through filters (p. 5-25).

variables.AOS: apparent opening size of the geotextile
variables.D85: soil particle size for which 85% are smaller
